claims.statement: One row is one account-balance snapshot, keyed by accountbalancesnode; this is the table's primary key.
One row is one analytics-indicator snapshot, keyed by analyticsindicatorsnode, linked 1:1 to a marketdata row and a marketstats row.
One row is one fee line associated with an order; an order can have more than one fee line since fees has 1,000 rows against 999 orders with a 100% join match.
One row is one market-data snapshot, keyed by marketdatanode, referenced 1:1 by a marketstats row and an analyticsindicators row.
One row is one market-statistics snapshot, keyed by marketstatsmark, chained to one marketdata row and one analyticsindicators row.
One row is one execution (fill or cancellation) event tied to an order.
One row is one order; orderspivot is the surrogate primary key, with 999 distinct orders in the table.
recordvault is the natural/business identifier for an order and is the column other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference via foreign key, not orderspivot.
One row is one risk/margin profile record tied to an order; since riskandmargin has 1,000 rows against 999 orders with full join match, some orders have more than one risk/margin row.
One row is one system-monitoring snapshot, linked 1:1 to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row is one user; usersnode and userstamp both uniquely identify a user, with 776 distinct users in the table.
In this data each accountbalances row has a distinct usertag, i.e. no user has more than one balance snapshot row; this may reflect how the data was generated rather than a guaranteed business rule.
In this data each order row has a distinct userlink, i.e. no user places more than one order; this looks like an artifact of the dataset rather than a guaranteed real-world rule.

Several real-valued measure columns (e.g. availsum, frozensum, margsum, realline, unrealline, walletsum, and similar columns in marketstats/orderexecutions/fees) are reported as row-unique by an automated check, but this uniqueness is almost certainly incidental to high-precision decimal values rather than a meaningful business key; they should not be treated as identifiers.

The users table covers only 776 user records; about 22% of the distinct user identifiers referenced from accountbalances.usertag and orders.userlink (e.g. 'U105156') do not exist in users, so joining orders or balances to users will silently drop those rows.
Orders only cover 12 trading pairs formed from 4 base assets (ADA, BTC, ETH, SOL) against 3 quote currencies (USD, USDT, USDC); no other markets are represented.
The fees table has 1,000 rows against only 999 orders, so at least one order has more than one associated fee row; aggregating fees per order must sum, not assume one row per order.
The riskandmargin table has 1,000 rows against only 999 orders, so at least one order has more than one risk/margin profile row.
acctscope records the trading account type a user is scoped to: Spot, Futures, or Options.
cancelnote records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty when the execution was not cancelled, which happens for 24.4% of rows.
exectune records whether a fill acted as Taker or Maker; it is empty for 31.1% of rows, presumably executions that never filled.
dealedge records the order side: Buy or Sell.
feecoin records the currency the fee was charged in (USDT, USD, or USDC); totals in feetotal are not directly comparable or additive across rows with different feecoin without currency conversion.
feerange is a fee-tier bucket label (Tier1 through Tier4), presumably reflecting a volume- or account-based pricing tier.
fundspot is a timestamp marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken, with observed values clustered on 2025-02-19 at hourly intervals.
mktnote records the traded market/symbol pair, e.g. ADA-USDC, BTC-USDT.
orderbase records the channel an order was submitted from: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle state: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune records the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
wsstate records the websocket connection status at the time of the snapshot: Connected or Disconnected.
fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate that can be negative or positive; the two 'format classes' found by automated checks are an artifact of the minus sign, not two different kinds of data.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure that can be negative (price fell) or positive (price rose); the detected format split is caused by the minus sign, not by mixed data types.
mkteffect is a signed measure of market impact that can be negative or positive; the detected format split is an artifact of the minus sign.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio that can be negative or positive depending on direction of slippage; the detected format split is an artifact of the minus sign.

realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed value: negative values represent a realised loss and positive values a realised gain; the detected 'format split' is simply due to the minus sign on losses.

unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed value: negative values represent an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain; the detected 'format split' is simply due to the minus sign on losses.
walletsum is derived as availsum + frozensum; it holds exactly for all 1,000 non-zero rows, so walletsum is a computed total and should not be summed alongside its components.

exectimespan is mostly equal to apilatmark + queueline (90.1% of non-zero rows), but for about 9.9% of rows it exceeds that sum, implying an additional, unrecorded latency component contributes to execution time for those rows.

'Execution time' is recorded as exectimespan; it equals 'API latency' (apilatmark) plus 'queueing' (queueline) for most rows, but for roughly 10% of rows it includes an additional component not represented by those two fields, so treating execution time as just latency+queueing underestimates it for those rows.
'API latency' refers to apilatmark, which is only a component of total execution time (exectimespan), not the whole of it.
'Queueing' refers to queueline, which is only a component of total execution time (exectimespan), not the whole of it.
'Wallet balance' is walletsum, defined strictly as availsum + frozensum; it excludes margsum (margin funds), so margin balances are not part of what 'wallet balance' covers.

'Trading fees' refers to fees.feetotal, the gross fee charged per fee line; it is stored separately from rebtotal (rebate) and is not netted against it, and an order may have more than one fee line to sum.
'Realised profit and loss' is accountbalances.realline, a signed figure distinct from unrealline (unrealised P&L); negative values are realised losses and positive values are realised gains.

claims.statement: Each row of accountbalances is one account-balance snapshot/record for a user, identified by accountbalancesnode.
Each row of analyticsindicators is one analytics-indicator record, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
Each row of fees is one fee record associated with an order, identified by feesnode.
Each row of marketdata is one market-data snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
Each row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, identified by marketstatsmark and linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot.
Each row of orderexecutions is one execution/fill event belonging to a single order, identified by orderexecmark.
recordvault is the natural, non-null identifier of one order row; the surrogate key orderspivot likewise uniquely identifies the 999 order rows, so both describe the same one-row-per-order grain.
Each row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record tied to one order, identified by riskandmarginpivot.
Each row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, identified by systemmonitoringpivot and linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
userstamp (equivalently usersnode) uniquely identifies one user record; the users table holds 776 distinct users.

The users table covers only 776 user records. About 22.3-22.4% of the user references found in orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag point to user identifiers that do not exist in users, so the table is a partial population that omits many users who are active elsewhere in the data.
dealedge encodes the trade direction of an order: Sell or Buy.
orderflow encodes the lifecycle status of an order: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune encodes the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan encodes the order's time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
orderbase encodes the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
feerange encodes a fee tier label applied to the trade: Tier1 through Tier4.
feecoin identifies the currency in which the fee is denominated: USDT, USD, or USDC.
acctscope encodes the account's trading scope/type: Spot, Futures, or Options.
wsstate records the websocket connection status: Connected or Disconnected.

cancelnote records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for 24.4% of rows, meaning no cancellation reason applies, presumably because the execution was not cancelled.
exectune classifies a fill as Maker or Taker; it is empty for 31.1% of rows, meaning those executions were not assigned a maker/taker classification (for example, unfilled or cancelled orders).
realline stores realised profit and loss as a signed quantity: negative values represent realised losses and positive values represent realised gains.

unrealline stores unrealised profit and loss as a signed quantity: negative values represent unrealised losses and positive values represent unrealised gains, distinct from the realised figure in realline.
fundrate is a signed funding rate: positive and negative values both occur, indicating the direction of the funding payment.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change: positive values indicate a price increase and negative values a decrease over the day.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure, taking both positive and negative values.

claims.statement: Each row is one account balance snapshot, one per account/user tag.
Each row is one analytics-indicator record tied to exactly one marketdata row and one marketstats row.
Each row is one fee (and paired rebate) record associated with an order.
Each row is one market-data snapshot (order book depth capture).
Each row is one market statistics snapshot (funding, volume, supply, etc.), linked one-to-one to a marketdata row.
Each row is one order execution/fill (or cancellation) event belonging to an order.
Each row is one order record; recordvault is an alternate natural-key column for the same order, referenced as a foreign key from fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin.
Each row is one risk/margin profile record tied to exactly one order.
Each row is one system-monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
Each row is one user; userstamp is the natural key referenced by orders and accountbalances.

The users table holds only 776 distinct users, fewer than the distinct user identifiers referenced from orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag; it does not cover every user that appears elsewhere in the data.
About 22.3% of orders reference a user who is not present in the users table; an inner join between orders and users silently drops these orders.
About 22.4% of account balance rows reference a user who is not present in the users table; an inner join to users silently drops these rows.

Orders has 999 rows, one fewer than the 1,000-row count found in the related accountbalances, fees, orderexecutions, marketstats, marketdata, analyticsindicators and systemmonitoring tables, suggesting the orders table may be missing a record present elsewhere in the system.
acctscope holds the account-type scope: Spot, Futures, or Options.
cancelnote holds the cancellation reason code (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is populated only when the order/execution was cancelled, and left empty otherwise.
exectune holds the maker/taker execution role (Taker, Maker); it is empty for rows where no fill/execution occurred.
dealedge holds the trade direction flag: Buy or Sell.
feecoin holds the settlement currency code of the fee: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange holds a fee tier bucket: Tier1 through Tier4.
mktnote holds the traded market/pair symbol, e.g. BTC-USD, ADA-USDC.
orderbase holds the channel through which the order originated: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow holds the order lifecycle status: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune holds the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan holds the order's time-in-force code: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
wsstate holds the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot holds a full funding-snapshot timestamp string rather than a short code, despite its declared size; only 8 distinct hourly timestamps appear.

realline is the realised profit and loss value for the account; it is a signed real number where negative values indicate a realised loss and positive values a realised gain. The apparent split into 'numeric' and 'alphanumeric' format classes in automated checks is an artifact of the minus sign, not two genuinely different kinds of value.

unrealline is the unrealised profit and loss value for the account, a signed real number (negative = unrealised loss, positive = unrealised gain), paralleling realline. The reported 'format classes' split is an artifact of the minus sign.

fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate (can be negative or positive); the 'numeric' vs 'alphanumeric' split reported by checks is caused by the minus sign on negative values, not a true mix of data kinds.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact metric (can be negative or positive); the reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not a true mix of data kinds.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure (can be negative or positive); the reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not a true mix of data kinds.
slipratio is a signed slippage-ratio figure (can be negative or positive); the reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not a true mix of data kinds.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON object with nested sentiment sub-fields (e.g. instflow), not a single scalar or category; grouping on the raw text therefore fragments identical underlying records into many spurious 'variants'.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON object with nested order-book depth sub-fields (e.g. askdepth), not a single scalar or category; grouping on the raw text therefore fragments identical underlying records into many spurious 'variants'.

Execution time (exectimespan) equals API latency (apilatmark) plus queueing time (queueline) for about 90% of rows; for the remaining roughly 10% the recorded execution time exceeds that sum, meaning at least one further unmodeled component contributes to execution time on those rows.

Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived column equal to availsum (available) plus frozensum (frozen) for all non-zero rows; summing walletsum together with availsum and/or frozensum double-counts the balance.
"Realised profit and loss" refers specifically to accountbalances.realline, a signed amount distinct from the unrealised figure stored in unrealline; it does not include unrealised gains/losses.
"Trading fees" corresponds to fees.feetotal and excludes any rebate amount, which is recorded separately in rebtotal; combining the two would misstate the fee actually charged.

A cancellation reason (cancelnote) is only defined for executions that were actually cancelled; for the roughly 24% of rows with no cancellation, the term does not apply and the field is empty rather than meaning 'no reason'.
The maker/taker role (exectune) is only defined for executions that actually produced a fill; for the roughly 31% of rows with no fill, the term does not apply.
Fees rows (1,000) outnumber orders rows (999) by many-to-one, so not every order necessarily has exactly one fee row; some orders may have zero or multiple fee rows.
Orderexecutions rows (1,000) outnumber orders rows (999) by many-to-one, so not every order necessarily has exactly one execution row; some orders may have zero or multiple execution rows.
Riskandmargin rows (1,000) outnumber orders rows (999) by many-to-one, so not every order necessarily has exactly one risk/margin row; some orders may have zero or multiple risk rows.

claims.statement: One row of accountbalances is one account-balance record (presumably a balance snapshot for a user/account), identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators is one analytics/sentiment indicator snapshot, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.

One row of fees is one fee-charge event. Fees is not one row per order: 1,000 fee rows all match orders.recordvault but orders has only 999 rows, so at least one order has more than one associated fee row.
One row of marketdata is one order-book/quote-depth snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, identified by marketstatsmark.

One row of orderexecutions is one execution/fill event. Multiple execution rows can belong to the same order (e.g. partial fills): 1,000 execution rows all match orders.recordvault but orders has only 999 rows.
One row of orders is one order record; orderspivot (surrogate) and recordvault (business/order id used by other tables as foreign key) both identify the same 999 order rows.

One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile entry. It is not strictly one row per order: 1,000 rows all match orders.recordvault but orders has only 999 rows, so at least one order has more than one risk/margin entry.

One row of systemmonitoring is one monitoring event, in a one-to-one relationship with analyticsindicators (same row count, full match via aitrack), suggesting the two tables share a common snapshot grain.
One row of users is one user; usersnode (surrogate) and userstamp (business user id referenced by other tables) both identify the same 776 user rows.

The users table does not cover all user identifiers that appear elsewhere in the database: about 22% of orders.userlink values and about 22% of accountbalances.usertag values reference a userstamp that does not exist in users, so joining orders or balances to users will silently drop roughly a fifth of activity.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum; it is not an independent balance and should not be summed alongside its components.
The business term 'wallet balance' is defined as availsum + frozensum (walletsum); it excludes margsum (margin balance) and the realised/unrealised P&L lines, which are tracked separately.

exectimespan equals apilatmark + queueline for 90.1% of non-zero rows; for the remaining ~9.9% it exceeds that sum, meaning a further, unrecorded time component contributes to execution time on those rows.

'Execution time' maps to exectimespan, 'API latency' maps to apilatmark, and 'queueing' maps to queueline, but execution time = API latency + queueing only holds for about 90% of rows; for the rest execution time includes extra time not captured by those two named components.
'Realised profit and loss' maps to accountbalances.realline and is a signed amount: negative values are losses, positive values are gains; it is distinct from the unrealised P&L stored in unrealline.
realline holds signed decimal amounts (both positive and negative), not pure integers despite its declared integer type; the sign indicates gain versus loss.
unrealline holds signed decimal amounts representing unrealised profit and loss, with negative values indicating unrealised losses and positive values indicating unrealised gains.
fundrate is a signed funding rate; negative values represent a negative funding rate, not a different kind of data.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change; negative values indicate a price decrease over the day, positive values an increase.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative values indicate slippage in the opposite direction from positive values (e.g. favorable vs unfavorable slippage).
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure; negative and positive values denote opposite directions of impact, not different data types.

cancelnote holds the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested) when an execution was cancelled; it is empty for executions that were not cancelled, so averages or grouping over it silently exclude the ~24% non-cancelled rows.
exectune holds the execution liquidity role (Taker, Maker); it is empty for roughly 31% of rows, presumably executions for which this role was not recorded (e.g. not yet matched or not applicable).
acctscope classifies a user's account by trading product scope: Spot, Futures, or Options.
feecoin is the currency in which a trading fee was charged: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange denotes the fee tier applied to a trade: Tier1 through Tier4.

'Trading fees' maps to fees.feetotal, the fee amount charged on a fill; this is tracked separately from rebates (rebtotal), so it is unclear whether the business term 'trading fees' is meant gross of or net of rebates.
fundspot stores the full timestamp of a funding-rate snapshot (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46'), despite being declared as a short text(6) field; only 8 distinct hourly snapshot times appear in the data.
dealedge records the side of a trade: Buy or Sell.
mktnote holds the traded instrument/market pair symbol, limited to 12 crypto-fiat/stablecoin pairs built from ADA, BTC, ETH, SOL against USD, USDT, USDC.
orderbase records the channel an order originated from: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow records order status/lifecycle state: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune records the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan records the order's time-in-force instruction: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
wsstate records the websocket connection state at the time of the monitoring row: Connected or Disconnected.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a nested JSON blob of sentiment metrics (e.g. flow/instflow), not a simple code; near-duplicate JSON strings for the same underlying value exist as separate stored values, so grouping or matching on the raw text undercounts true distinct sentiment states.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a nested JSON blob of order-book depth (e.g. askdepth), not a simple code; near-duplicate JSON strings for the same underlying depth value exist as separate stored values, so grouping or matching on the raw text undercounts true distinct depth states.

claims.statement: One row of accountbalances is one account-balance snapshot, identified by accountbalancesnode (the declared primary key).
About 22.4% of accountbalances rows carry a usertag that does not match any row in users, so the users table does not cover all account holders that have balance records.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum, not an independently observed quantity.
"Wallet balance" refers to walletsum, which is defined strictly as available funds plus frozen funds; it excludes margin (margsum), which is tracked separately.
realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed amount, with negative values representing a realised loss and positive values a realised gain.
unrealline is likewise a signed amount, almost certainly representing unrealised profit and loss, with negative values an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain.
One row of analyticsindicators is one computed analytics/sentiment record, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.

Each analyticsindicators row links to exactly one marketdata row (via mdataref) and one marketstats row (via mstatsref), both matching 100% and one-to-one, so this table is an enrichment of marketdata/marketstats rather than an independent population.

market_sentiment_indicators holds a free-form JSON blob (e.g. a "flow.instflow" field) rather than a coded category; apparent repeated value families are coincidental numeric matches, not meaningful groupings.
One row of fees is one fee/rebate assessment, identified by feesnode.
Every fees row links to an existing orders row via orderslink (100% match, many-to-one), so fees are fully scoped to known orders.
feerange holds a fee-tier code (Tier1 through Tier4), not a continuous range value.
feecoin holds the settlement currency of the fee (USDT, USD, USDC).
"Trading fees" refers to feetotal, the amount charged to the account; it is distinct from rebtotal, a rebate amount that should not be netted into feetotal without being explicit about it.
One row of marketdata is one order-book depth snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
Every marketstats row links to exactly one marketdata row via mdlink (100% match), suggesting a one-to-one pairing between the two tables rather than marketdata existing independently.
quote_depth_snapshot holds a free-form JSON blob (e.g. an "askdepth" field); apparent repeated value families are coincidental and not a meaningful category.
One row of marketstats is one market statistics snapshot (daily/period stats for an instrument), identified by marketstatsmark.
Every marketstats row has a matching marketdata row via mdlink (100%), so marketstats never references a missing snapshot.
fundrate is a signed funding rate: negative values indicate longs pay shorts (or vice versa) rather than two different kinds of data.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change: negative values mean the price fell, positive values mean it rose.
fundspot stores a timestamp of the funding snapshot; the stored values are full datetime strings even though the column is declared as a 6-character field, so truncation or mismatch risk exists.
One row of orderexecutions is one execution/fill (or cancellation) event against an order, identified by orderexecmark.
Every orderexecutions row links to an existing orders row via ordersmark (100% match, many-to-one), so all executions are scoped to known orders.
cancelnote holds the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for the 24.4% of executions that were not cancelled, not missing data.
exectune holds a Maker/Taker execution-role flag; it is empty for the 31.1% of executions where no fill occurred (e.g. pure cancellations), not a third category of role.

One row of orders is one order; orderspivot is the surrogate row key (999 distinct values across 999 rows), while recordvault is the natural/business order identifier referenced by fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin.
dealedge holds the trade direction, Buy or Sell.
orderflow holds the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune holds the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan holds the order's time-in-force code: GTC, IOC, FOK, or GTD.
orderbase holds the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote holds the traded instrument/market symbol, e.g. ADA-USDC, limited to a small set of crypto trading pairs.
About 22.32% of orders rows carry a userlink that does not match any row in users, so the users table does not cover all customers who placed orders.
One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record, identified by riskandmarginpivot.
Every riskandmargin row links to an existing orders row via ordervault (100% match, many-to-one), so risk profiles are fully scoped to known orders.
risk_margin_profile holds a free-form JSON blob of risk/margin details rather than a coded category.
One row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, identified by systemmonitoringpivot; aitrack is also unique per row and is a one-to-one foreign key to analyticsindicators.
Every systemmonitoring row links to exactly one analyticsindicators row via aitrack (100% match), indicating a one-to-one pairing between monitoring snapshots and analytics records.
wsstate holds the websocket connectivity state, Connected or Disconnected.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure, with negative and positive values indicating direction of effect rather than two kinds of data.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio, with negative values indicating slippage against the order and positive values favourable slippage.

exectimespan ('execution time') equals apilatmark ('API latency') plus queueline ('queueing') for 90.1% of non-zero rows; for the remaining ~9.9% it is larger than that sum, meaning at least one further, uncaptured component contributes to execution time on those rows.
"Execution time" is only fully explained by "API latency" plus "queueing" for about 90% of rows; treating execution time as always equal to that sum will understate it for the other ~10%.
One row of users is one user account, identified by usersnode (and equivalently by userstamp, its 36-character business identifier); the table holds 776 distinct users.

The users table is an incomplete directory of all users with activity: roughly 22% of the distinct user tags referenced in orders and accountbalances do not exist in users, so about 224 active users are missing from this table.
acctscope holds the account's trading scope/product type: Spot, Futures, or Options.

claims.statement: One row of accountbalances is one account-balance record, identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators is one analytics-indicator snapshot, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row of fees is one fee record, identified by feesnode.
One row of marketdata is one market-data snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, identified by marketstatsmark.
One row of orderexecutions is one order-execution (fill) event, identified by orderexecmark.
One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record, identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row of systemmonitoring is one system-monitoring snapshot, identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row of users is one user, identified by usersnode (and equivalently by userstamp); the table holds 776 users.
One row of orders is one order, identified by orderspivot; the natural key recordvault has the same cardinality and is the key referenced by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin.

The users table does not cover all user identifiers that appear in orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag: about 22% of referencing rows point to a userstamp not present in users, so users is an incomplete population relative to the activity tables.

marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators and systemmonitoring each have exactly 1,000 rows and are fully, uniquely chained to one another (100% match, one-to-one), suggesting these four tables represent the same 1,000 underlying snapshots split across tables rather than independent populations.

orders holds 999 order records; fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin each match 100% of their rows back to an order, so those tables are strict extensions of the orders population with no orphaned records.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order, taking only the values Sell and Buy.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records a time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.

cancelnote holds a cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for executions that were not cancelled (about 24.4% of rows), so emptiness is meaningful, not missing data.
exectune records the liquidity role of the fill, Taker or Maker; it is empty (about 31.1% of rows) when the execution has no assigned role, e.g. not matched or cancelled before any fill.
feerange records a fee tier level: Tier1 through Tier4.
feecoin records the currency the fee was charged in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
wsstate records the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
acctscope records the account's product scope: Spot, Futures, or Options.

fundspot stores a full timestamp (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46') rather than the 6-character code its declared type suggests, and only takes 8 distinct hourly values, so it likely marks the hour of a funding-rate snapshot rather than a short status code.

realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed real number: negative values represent a realised loss and positive values a realised gain; the apparent split into two automated 'formats' is only the minus sign on loss values, not two different kinds of data.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed real number: negative values represent an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain; the two 'formats' flagged are just the sign.

fundrate is a signed funding-rate percentage; negative values indicate a funding payment in one direction (e.g. shorts paid by longs) and positive the other, not two distinct data kinds despite the automated format split.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change; negative values mean the price fell over the day and positive values mean it rose, with the automated 'format' split simply reflecting the sign.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact value whose sign indicates the direction of the impact; the automated format split again reflects only the minus sign.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative and positive values indicate the direction (favorable vs unfavorable) of slippage, not two separate kinds of value.
walletsum (wallet balance) is a derived column equal to availsum + frozensum for every non-zero row; it should not be summed alongside its components or it will double count.

exectimespan (execution time) equals apilatmark (API latency) plus queueline (queueing) for about 90% of non-zero rows; for the remaining ~10% exectimespan exceeds that sum, meaning execution time includes at least one further, unstored component for those rows.

"Wallet balance" is bounded to available plus frozen funds (availsum + frozensum); it excludes margin (margsum) and any realised/unrealised P&L (realline, unrealline), which are tracked as separate quantities.
"Trading fees" refers to feetotal as charged; it is stored separately from rebtotal (rebate), so the term does not automatically net out rebates unless explicitly combined.
"Realised profit and loss" is exactly the value stored in accountbalances.realline, a signed amount where sign indicates gain or loss.
"Execution time" is defined as API latency (apilatmark) plus queueing (queueline) in about 90% of rows, but for roughly 10% of rows the term's full scope extends beyond these two stored components.
"API latency" maps to systemmonitoring.apilatmark, one of the two named components of execution time.
"Queueing" maps to systemmonitoring.queueline, the other named component of execution time.

analyticsindicators.market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON-like structure whose first field repeats across many rows with slightly different full payloads (199 value families with multiple variants), so grouping or counting on the raw text will split records that share the same sentiment reading into separate groups.

marketdata.quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON-like structure whose leading field repeats with varying full payloads (263 value families with multiple variants), so grouping or counting on the raw text will split records that share the same depth reading into separate categories.

unrealline is a signed numeric amount representing unrealised profit/loss, with the reported two-class split being an artifact of negative signs rather than two distinct kinds of data.

slipratio is a signed slippage ratio (positive or negative slippage); the two reported formats are an artifact of sign, not distinct kinds of data.

claims.statement: Each row of accountbalances is one account-balance snapshot/record, one per user wallet state captured.
Each row of systemmonitoring is one system/API performance monitoring event, optionally linked to one analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
Each row of analyticsindicators is one analytics-indicator snapshot, tied to exactly one marketdata row and one marketstats row.
Each row of fees is one fee (and matching rebate) assessment tied to a single order via orderslink; an order can have more than one fee row.
Each row of orderexecutions is one execution/fill event belonging to a single order via ordersmark; an order can have more than one execution row.
Each row of marketdata is one quote/order-book depth snapshot.
Each row of marketstats is one market-statistics snapshot, optionally tied to one marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
Each row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile record tied to a single order via ordervault; an order can have more than one such row.
orderspivot is the surrogate numeric key of orders; one row of orders is one order.
recordvault is the business/order identifier that fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin reference; it uniquely identifies one order row.
userstamp (with surrogate usersnode) uniquely identifies one user; the users table holds 776 distinct users.

The users table does not cover every user that appears elsewhere: about 22.3% of orders.userlink values and 22.4% of accountbalances.usertag values reference user identifiers that do not exist in users, so those users' orders and balances cannot be joined to a user record.

orders has 999 rows while fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin and accountbalances each have 1,000 rows; some orders have more than one associated fee/execution/risk row (a many-to-one relationship), not a coverage gap on the orders side.

cancelnote is populated only for executions that were actually cancelled; roughly a quarter of execution rows have no cancellation reason because they were not cancelled, and any aggregate over cancelnote silently excludes them.
exectune (maker/taker tag) is missing for about 31% of execution rows, presumably for executions that did not actually fill or were not tagged; aggregates over exectune silently exclude those rows.

marketdata, marketstats and analyticsindicators form a separate chain of market-level snapshots (linked via mdlink/mdataref/mstatsref) describing overall market/instrument conditions; they are not tied to any specific order or user.
acctscope records the trading account type a user operates: Spot, Futures, or Options.
dealedge records the side of the order: Buy or Sell.
orderflow records the lifecycle status of an order: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force instruction: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase records the channel/platform through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote records the traded instrument/market pair, covering 12 crypto pairs across ADA, ETH, SOL, BTC quoted against USD/USDT/USDC.
exectune records whether the fill was executed as Taker or Maker; it is null when the order was not (yet) filled.
cancelnote records the reason an order execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is null when the execution was not cancelled.
feerange records the fee tier bracket applied to the trade: Tier1 through Tier4.
feecoin records the currency the trading fee was charged in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
wsstate records the websocket connection state at monitoring time: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot stores a timestamp (one of 8 hourly snapshots on 2025-02-19) marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken, not a free-form category.

fundrate holds a signed decimal funding rate that can be negative or positive; the two 'format classes' flagged by automated checks are an artifact of the minus sign being treated as non-numeric, not two different kinds of data.
mkteffect holds a signed numeric market-impact figure (negative and positive); the two detected format classes are only the sign difference, not distinct kinds of data.
priceshiftday holds a signed daily price-change figure (negative and positive); the apparent two-format split found by checks is just the presence/absence of a minus sign.
realline stores realised profit and loss for the account, a signed amount that can be negative (loss) or positive (profit); the two detected 'format classes' are just the sign.
unrealline stores the unrealised profit and loss for the account, a signed amount distinct from the realised figure in realline; the detected format split is just the sign.
slipratio holds a signed slippage ratio that can be negative or positive; the two detected format classes are only the sign difference.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON document of nested sentiment/flow metrics rather than a simple category; the repeated 'variants' found by checks are distinct JSON documents sharing a numeric prefix, not true duplicate categories.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON document of nested order-book depth figures rather than a simple category; the 'variant' groups found by checks are distinct JSON documents sharing a numeric prefix, not duplicate categories.
walletsum (wallet balance) is a derived column equal to availsum + frozensum, confirmed exactly on all 1,000 non-zero rows; it is not an independently stored balance.

exectimespan (execution time) equals apilatmark (API latency) plus queueline (queueing) for 90.1% of non-zero rows; for the remaining 9.9% exectimespan exceeds that sum, implying an unmodeled extra latency component.
'Wallet balance' is defined as available funds plus frozen funds (availsum+frozensum); it excludes the margin balance (margsum) and both the realised and unrealised P&L lines (realline, unrealline).

'Realised profit and loss' refers specifically to accountbalances.realline and is distinct from the unrealised figure held separately in accountbalances.unrealline; it can be negative (loss) or positive (gain).

'Execution time' is only fully explained as 'API latency' (apilatmark) plus 'queueing' (queueline) for about 90% of rows; for roughly 9.9% of rows the recorded execution time is larger than that sum, so the two named components do not account for all of execution time on those rows.
'Trading fees' corresponds to fees.feetotal and is kept separate from any rebate amount stored in rebtotal; the two are not netted into a single figure in this data.

claims.statement: One row represents a single account balance snapshot, nominally one per user tag (usertag is also unique across the 1,000 rows).
One row is a single analytics-indicator snapshot that joins exactly one marketdata row and one marketstats row (mdataref and mstatsref are each unique and fully matched).
One row is a single fee (and rebate) record associated with one order via orderslink.
One row is a single market data snapshot (order-book depth) at a point in time.
One row is a single market statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata row via mdlink.
One row is a single order execution (fill or cancellation) event tied to one order via ordersmark.

One row is a single order; recordvault (a text key, 999 distinct values over 999 rows) is the natural key used by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin to reference orders, alongside the integer surrogate key orderspivot.
One row is a single risk/margin profile tied to one order via ordervault.
One row is a single system monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one to one analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row is a single user; userstamp (776 distinct values over 776 rows) is the natural key referenced by accountbalances.usertag and orders.userlink.

The users table does not cover all users referenced elsewhere: about 22.3-22.4% of orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag values (e.g. 'U105156') have no matching userstamp in users, so roughly a fifth of users who placed orders or hold balances are missing from this table.
acctscope records the user's account type/scope with three categories: Spot, Futures, and Options.
dealedge is the trade direction of the order: Buy or Sell.
orderflow is the order's lifecycle status, with values New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, and Cancelled.
ordertune is the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan is the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase is the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
mktnote holds the traded market/pair symbol (e.g. ADA-USDC, ETH-USD, BTC-USDT), one of 12 trading pairs.
cancelnote holds the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested) and is empty when the execution was not a cancellation.
exectune records the liquidity role of the execution, Maker or Taker, and is empty for executions where that role does not apply (e.g. not yet filled).
feecoin is the currency the fee is denominated/paid in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange is a fee tier label (Tier1-Tier4) determining the fee/rebate rate applied.
wsstate is the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot is a timestamp marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken; it takes only a handful of distinct hourly values in this data.

realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed amount; negative values denote a realised loss and positive values a realised gain. The 'numeric'/'alphanumeric' split flagged by automated checks is just the presence of a leading minus sign, not two distinct kinds of data.

unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed amount; negative values denote an unrealised loss and positive an unrealised gain. The reported format split is just the sign, not two different data types.
fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure; the 'numeric' vs 'alphanumeric' split reported is simply positive vs negative values, not distinct categories.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change figure; the format split reported is positive vs negative values, not distinct categories.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact metric; the reported format split is positive vs negative values, not distinct categories.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; the reported format split is positive vs negative values, not distinct categories.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON blob of sentiment sub-metrics (e.g. instflow) rather than a categorical code; near-duplicate 'variants' found by text grouping are different JSON payloads sharing a similar prefix, not misspellings of one category.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON blob of order-book depth sub-metrics (e.g. askdepth) rather than a categorical code; near-duplicate 'variants' are different JSON payloads sharing a similar prefix, not misspellings of one category.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is exactly availsum + frozensum for all rows; it is a derived total, not an independent balance, so summing it with its components double-counts.

Execution time (exectimespan) equals API latency (apilatmark) plus queueing (queueline) for about 90% of rows, but for roughly 10% of rows it is larger than that sum, meaning at least one further, unrecorded component also contributes to execution time.

"Execution time" is not fully defined as API latency plus queueing; for about 10% of rows the measured execution time exceeds that sum, so the term includes additional unmeasured delay beyond API latency and queueing.
The cancellation-reason term only applies to executions that were actually cancelled; it is blank (not a fourth reason) for the 24.4% of executions that were not cancelled.
The maker/taker execution-role term does not apply to the 31.1% of execution rows where it is blank, presumably orders not yet matched or not applicable to a role.

claims.statement: One row represents one account balance record (one snapshot of a user's balances).
recordvault is the natural/business key for an order and is the column other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference; one row of orders is one order.
orderspivot is a surrogate integer identifier for the same order grain as recordvault; one row is one order.
One row is one fee (and possibly associated rebate) charge event tied to an order.
One row is one market-data snapshot (quote depth at a point in time).
One row is one market-statistics snapshot, standing in a one-to-one relationship with a marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
One row is one analytics snapshot pairing exactly one marketdata record and one marketstats record (both links are unique/one-to-one).
One row is one execution (fill/cancel) event against an order.
One row is one risk/margin profile snapshot tied to an order.
One row is one system-monitoring snapshot, in a one-to-one relationship with one analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
One row is one user; userstamp is the user's natural identifier, referenced from orders and accountbalances.

The users table covers only 776 users. Roughly 22% of orders (userlink) and 22% of accountbalances (usertag) reference user identifiers, e.g. 'U105156', that do not exist in users, so users does not cover all individuals who placed orders or hold balances.
orders only covers 12 trading-pair markets formed from base assets ADA, BTC, ETH, SOL against quote currencies USD, USDT, USDC; no other instruments appear in the data.
Fees are denominated only in USDT, USD, or USDC; no other settlement currencies occur.
User account scope covers only Spot, Futures, and Options categories; no other account types exist.
systemmonitoring and analyticsindicators are in complete one-to-one correspondence (1,000 rows each, 100% matched), so every monitoring snapshot has exactly one analytics snapshot and vice versa.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order, with values Sell and Buy.
orderflow is the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune is the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan is a time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
orderbase is the channel through which the order was submitted: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
exectune marks the execution role (Maker or Taker); it is null (31.1% of rows) when the concept does not apply, e.g. orders not filled.
cancelnote records the reason an order execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is null (24.4%) when the execution was not cancelled.
feerange is a fee tier code: Tier1 through Tier4.
wsstate records websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot is a timestamp marking when the funding-rate snapshot was taken; the data appears to span only a handful of hourly snapshots on 2025-02-19.

realline is a signed amount: positive values indicate realised profit, negative values realised loss. The automated check's 'alphanumeric' bucket is simply values with a leading minus sign, not a distinct code system.
unrealline is a signed amount representing unrealised profit (positive) or loss (negative); the two 'format classes' flagged are simply positive vs negative numbers.
fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate; the flagged 'format classes' are positive vs negative numbers, not different kinds of data.
priceshiftday is a signed decimal daily price change; negative values mean the price fell.
mkteffect is a signed numeric market-impact metric; negative values indicate downward impact.
slipratio is a signed numeric slippage ratio; negative values indicate slippage in the opposite direction.
walletsum is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum, holding for all non-zero rows (100%). It is not an independent balance.

exectimespan equals apilatmark + queueline for 90.1% of non-zero rows, but for the remaining ~9.9% exectimespan exceeds that sum, implying an additional unmeasured component contributes to execution time for those rows.
The business term 'wallet balance' is defined as availsum plus frozensum (walletsum); it excludes margin (margsum) and realised/unrealised P&L (realline/unrealline).
'Realised profit and loss' is defined as the value stored in accountbalances.realline, a signed amount where negative is a loss and positive a gain.
'Trading fees' most plausibly refers to fees.feetotal, the fee amount charged; rebtotal is a separate rebate credited back and is likely not included under 'trading fees'.

'Execution time' corresponds to systemmonitoring.exectimespan, nominally composed of 'API latency' (apilatmark) plus 'queueing' (queueline), but this two-term decomposition under-explains about 9.9% of non-zero rows where exectimespan is larger than the sum.
'API latency' corresponds to systemmonitoring.apilatmark, one of the two measured components that normally sum to execution time.
'Queueing' corresponds to systemmonitoring.queueline, the other measured component that normally sums to execution time together with API latency.

claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance snapshot for a single user; the table also holds exactly one such row per usertag value present in it.
One row represents one analytics/sentiment computation tied to a specific marketdata and marketstats snapshot.
One row represents one fee (and associated rebate) charge record, linked to a single order.
One row represents one market order-book/quote depth snapshot.
One row represents one aggregated market-statistics snapshot (volume, funding, supply metrics) for a point in time, linked to one marketdata snapshot.
One row represents one execution (fill or cancellation event) of an order.
One row represents one order; recordvault is the natural/business key used by other tables to reference an order, while orderspivot is the surrogate key.
One row represents one risk/margin profile record associated with a single order.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot (API/latency/queue metrics), linked to one analyticsindicators record.
One row represents one user; userstamp is the business key and usersnode the surrogate key, both unique across 776 rows.

The users table covers only 776 distinct users, but about 22% of the userstamp values referenced from orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag do not exist in it, so users is missing roughly a fifth of the users that appear elsewhere in the data.

orders contains 999 order records; fees, orderexecutions, and riskandmargin each have 1,000 rows that all match an order via recordvault, implying orders can have more than one associated fee, execution, or risk-margin row (one order to many child rows), not a coverage gap in orders.

marketdata, marketstats, analyticsindicators, and systemmonitoring each hold 1,000 rows fully linked to one another (marketstats→marketdata, analyticsindicators→marketdata and marketstats, systemmonitoring→analyticsindicators all match 100%), suggesting these tables represent the same 1,000 point-in-time snapshots split across tables rather than independently-sized populations.
acctscope is a categorical account-type code with three values: Spot, Futures, Options.
cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); a null/empty value (24.4% of rows) means the execution was not cancelled.
exectune records the liquidity role of the fill (Maker or Taker); a null value (31.1% of rows) means no fill occurred yet or the role is not applicable.
dealedge records the trade direction, with two values: Buy and Sell.
feecoin records the currency the fee is denominated in, limited to USDT, USD, and USDC.
feerange is a fee-tier bucket with four levels: Tier1 through Tier4.
orderbase records the channel an order originated from: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, IOC, or FOK.
wsstate records the websocket connection status: Connected or Disconnected.
fundspot stores a timestamp (snapshot time) for the funding-rate observation, not a plain code, despite its short declared width.

realline holds a signed decimal value (realised profit and loss), with negative values representing losses and positive values representing gains; the apparent split between a 'numeric' and 'alphanumeric' format in checks is only an artifact of the minus sign, not two distinct kinds of data.

unrealline holds a signed decimal value (unrealised profit and loss), with negative values representing losses and positive values representing gains; the format split flagged by checks is caused by the minus sign, not a genuine category difference.

fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate (can be negative or positive); the 'numeric vs alphanumeric' split flagged by checks is an artifact of the minus sign on negative values, not two different data kinds.
priceshiftday is a signed decimal daily price change (can be negative or positive); the format split flagged by checks is an artifact of the minus sign, not a genuine category difference.
mkteffect is a signed decimal market-impact metric (can be negative or positive); the format split flagged by checks is an artifact of the minus sign.
slipratio is a signed decimal slippage ratio (can be negative or positive); the format split flagged by checks is an artifact of the minus sign.
walletsum (wallet balance) is a derived sum: walletsum = availsum + frozensum, holding for all 1,000 non-zero rows checked; margsum is not part of this total.

exectimespan (execution time) equals apilatmark (API latency) plus queueline (queueing) for about 90.1% of rows; for the remaining ~9.9% exectimespan exceeds that sum, indicating an additional, unrecorded latency component.
"Wallet balance" is defined as available funds plus frozen funds (availsum + frozensum); it excludes margin funds held in margsum.

"Execution time" is intended to equal "API latency" (apilatmark) plus "queueing" (queueline), but for about 1 in 10 rows the recorded execution time is larger than that sum, so for those rows the term includes additional unaccounted-for time beyond API latency and queueing.

"Realised profit and loss" is stored as a single signed value per account-balance row in realline, covering both gains (positive) and losses (negative); it is a distinct figure from unrealline (unrealised P&L).

"Trading fees" correspond to fees.feetotal, one row per fee charge linked to an order; no checked arithmetic relation ties feetotal to rebtotal/rebrate, so it is not established whether the rebate is netted into feetotal or reported separately.

One row of orderexecutions represents one execution/fill event against an order (consistent with partial-fill fields fillcount/remaincount); because 1,000 execution rows all match orders.recordvault while orders has only 999 rows, at least one order has more than one execution row.

One row of riskandmargin represents one risk/margin profile tied to an order; because 1,000 riskandmargin rows all match orders.recordvault while orders has only 999 rows, at least one order has more than one risk/margin profile row.
One row of users represents one user; userstamp is the business key used by accountbalances and orders to reference the user.

claims.statement: One row of accountbalances is one account balance record (one snapshot of a user's holdings), identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators is one analytics/indicator record tied to a single marketdata snapshot and a single marketstats snapshot, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row of fees is one fee (or rebate) assessment tied to a single order, identified by feesnode.
One row of marketdata is one quote-depth snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats is one market statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot via mdlink, identified by marketstatsmark.
One row of orderexecutions is one execution (or cancellation/fill) event belonging to one order, identified by orderexecmark.
One row of orders is one order, identified equivalently by the surrogate orderspivot and the natural key recordvault; the table holds 999 orders.
One row of riskandmargin is one risk/margin profile tied to a single order, identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row of systemmonitoring is one system/API monitoring record, linked one-to-one to an analyticsindicators record via aitrack, identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row of users is one user account, identified equivalently by the surrogate usersnode and the natural key userstamp; the table holds 776 users.

The users table does not cover every user referenced elsewhere: about 22% of the user identifiers used in orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag (roughly 223-224 of ~1,000 rows each) have no matching row in users, so joins to users silently drop those accounts.
usertag is unique within accountbalances, so each of the 1,000 account-balance rows belongs to a distinct user even though only 776 of those users exist in the users table.

Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived sum of availsum (available) and frozensum (frozen); it holds exactly for all non-zero rows, so summing walletsum together with availsum or frozensum double-counts.
"Wallet balance" is defined as available plus frozen funds only; it excludes margin funds (margsum) and realised/unrealised P&L lines (realline, unrealline), which are tracked separately.

Execution time (exectimespan) is approximately the sum of API latency (apilatmark) and queueing (queueline); this holds for 90.1% of non-zero rows but for the remaining rows the recorded execution time exceeds that sum, indicating an additional, unrecorded time component.
"Execution time" cannot be fully reconstructed from "API latency" plus "queueing" alone for about 9.9% of monitoring records; a further unmodeled contributor exists for those rows.
realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed figure: positive values represent realised gains and negative values represent realised losses.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed figure: positive values represent unrealised gains and negative values represent unrealised losses.
fundrate is a signed funding rate, taking both positive and negative values depending on which side (longs or shorts) pays funding.
priceshiftday is a signed day-over-day price change, taking both positive (price up) and negative (price down) values.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio, taking both positive and negative values depending on whether execution was worse or better than expected.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure, taking both positive and negative values.
acctscope records the account's trading scope, taking the values Spot, Futures, and Options.
cancelnote records the cancellation reason (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested) and is empty for executions that were not cancelled, not a missing-data gap.
exectune records whether an execution was a Taker or Maker fill, and is empty for executions that have not (yet) been matched, not a missing-data gap.
feecoin records the currency the fee was denominated/charged in, taking the values USDT, USD, and USDC.
feerange records a fee tier bucket (Tier1-Tier4) that the fee rate was drawn from.
"Trading fees" refers to feetotal, the amount charged to the user; rebtotal is a separate rebate/credit amount in the opposite direction and is not itself part of the fee charged.
fundspot holds one of 8 distinct timestamps, acting as a discrete funding-interval snapshot time rather than a continuous timestamp.
mktnote records the traded market/pair symbol (e.g. ADA-USDC, BTC-USD), with 12 distinct pairs observed.
orderbase records the channel/origin an order was placed through, taking the values Web, Mobile, Bot, and API.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status, taking the values Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, and New.
ordertune records the order type, taking the values Stop, StopLimit, Limit, and Market.
timespan records the order's time-in-force instruction, taking the values GTD, FOK, IOC, and GTC.
dealedge records the order's side/direction, taking the values Sell and Buy.
wsstate records the websocket connection state at the time of the monitoring record, taking the values Connected and Disconnected.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a JSON-serialized multi-field sentiment payload (e.g. nested flow/instflow metrics), not a single scalar category; grouping on raw text values fragments identical underlying records into many pseudo-distinct variants.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a JSON-serialized multi-field order-book depth payload (e.g. nested depth/askdepth metrics), not a single scalar category; grouping on raw text values fragments identical underlying records into many pseudo-distinct variants.

claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance snapshot for a user (wallet/available/frozen/margin amounts at a point in time); accountbalancesnode is the row identifier.
One row represents one analytics-indicator record tied one-to-one to a marketdata snapshot and a marketstats record.
One row represents one fee (or rebate) charge associated with an order; multiple fee rows can reference the same order.
One row represents one market-data snapshot (quote/depth data at a point in time).
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot, linked one-to-one to a marketdata row.
One row represents one execution (fill) event against an order; multiple execution rows can belong to the same order.

recordvault is the business key identifying one order; it is the column other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference, while orderspivot is a surrogate numeric key for the same 999-row grain.
One row represents one risk/margin profile entry for an order; more than one such row can reference the same order.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot, linked one-to-one via aitrack to an analyticsindicators record.
One row represents one user; userstamp is the natural key referenced by orders and accountbalances.

The users table holds only 776 user identities, but about 22% of the userstamp references made from orders and accountbalances point to user identifiers that do not exist in this table, so users is incomplete relative to the population actually referenced elsewhere; an inner join on userstamp silently drops those orders/balances.
acctscope records the account's trading scope/product type, taking the values Spot, Futures, or Options.
cancelnote records the reason an execution was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty when the execution was not cancelled (e.g. filled or still open).
exectune records the liquidity role of the fill, Taker or Maker; it is empty for roughly a third of rows, presumably executions that did not actually trade.
feecoin records the currency the fee amount is denominated in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange records a discrete fee-tier bucket (Tier1–Tier4) that the fee rate was drawn from.
fundspot is a snapshot timestamp (observed values are hourly timestamps on 2025-02-19) marking when the funding-rate figures were taken, not a free-form identifier.
mktnote records the traded market/pair symbol (e.g. ADA-USDC, BTC-USD); 12 pairs are in use across ADA, ETH, SOL, BTC against USD/USDC/USDT.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune records the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan records the order's time-in-force instruction code: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
dealedge records the order side, Buy or Sell.
wsstate records the websocket connectivity state at the time of the monitoring snapshot: Connected or Disconnected.

fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure; the automated check's split into 'numeric' and 'alphanumeric' shapes reflects only the presence of a minus sign, so negative values denote a negative funding rate rather than a different kind of data.

mkteffect is a signed integer indicating the direction of market impact (positive vs. negative effect); the 'alphanumeric' rows flagged by the automated check are simply negative values, not a separate category.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure; negative values indicate a price decrease and positive values a price increase over the day, not a distinct value type.
realline is a signed realised profit-and-loss figure; negative values represent a realised loss and positive values a realised gain.
unrealline is a signed unrealised profit-and-loss figure; negative values represent an unrealised loss and positive values an unrealised gain.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative and positive values denote opposite slippage directions rather than two different kinds of values.

market_sentiment_indicators stores a nested JSON object of sentiment/flow metrics (e.g. a 'flow.instflow' field) rather than a simple category; identical underlying metric values appear under multiple textual variants, so exact-string grouping fragments logically equal values.

quote_depth_snapshot stores a nested JSON object of order-book depth metrics (e.g. an 'depth.askdepth' field), not a simple category; identical underlying depth values appear as multiple textual variants, so exact-string grouping fragments logically equal values.
walletsum, the 'wallet balance', is a derived total equal to availsum plus frozensum for every row; it should not be summed alongside its components.

exectimespan ('execution time') equals apilatmark ('API latency') plus queueline ('queueing') for about 90% of rows; for the remaining ~10% exectimespan exceeds that sum, meaning at least one further, unrecorded component also contributes to execution time on those rows.
'Realised profit and loss' refers specifically to accountbalances.realline and excludes unrealised gains/losses, which are tracked separately in accountbalances.unrealline.
'Wallet balance' (walletsum) covers only available and frozen funds (availsum + frozensum); it excludes margin funds held in margsum, which is a separate balance component.
'Trading fees' corresponds to fees.feetotal, the fee charged; it excludes fees.rebtotal, which is a separate rebate/credit amount rather than a fee.

claims.statement: Each row of accountbalances represents one account-balance snapshot, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode.
Each row of analyticsindicators represents one analytics-indicator record, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
Each row of fees represents one fee (and optional rebate) assessment, uniquely identified by feesnode.
Each row of marketdata represents one quote-depth snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
Each row of marketstats represents one set of market statistics for a point in time, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark.
Each row of orderexecutions represents one execution (fill or cancellation) event tied to an order, uniquely identified by orderexecmark.
Each row of orders represents one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot (999 rows, 999 distinct values).
recordvault is the natural key of orders used by fees, orderexecutions and riskandmargin to reference a specific order; it is unique across the 999 order rows.
Each row of riskandmargin represents one risk/margin profile tied to an order, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot.
Each row of systemmonitoring represents one system-monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
Each row of users represents one user, uniquely identified by usersnode, with 776 distinct users in total.

The users table only covers 776 distinct users, but about 22% of accountbalances rows and 22% of orders rows reference a user identifier that is not present in users, so users is an incomplete population relative to the activity recorded elsewhere.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived quantity equal to availsum + frozensum; it is not an independent measurement.

The business term 'wallet balance' is defined as the sum of available funds and frozen funds (availsum + frozensum), so it already includes frozen balances and should not be added to either component again when aggregating.

Execution time (exectimespan) equals apilatmark + queueline for about 90% of the non-zero rows, but for the remaining ~10% it exceeds that sum, meaning at least one additional, unrecorded component contributes to execution time on those rows.

The business term 'execution time' is only fully explained by 'API latency' (apilatmark) plus 'queueing' (queueline) for about 90% of rows; for the remaining rows the term includes extra latency not captured by these two columns.
apilatmark is the stored measure of API latency, one of the additive components of execution time (exectimespan).
queueline is the stored measure of queueing, one of the additive components of execution time (exectimespan).

realline stores realised profit and loss as a signed amount, with negative values representing losses and positive values representing gains; its apparent 'alphanumeric' vs 'numeric' split is an artifact of the minus sign on negative values, not two different kinds of data.

unrealline stores unrealised profit and loss as a signed amount, with negative values representing unrealised losses and positive values representing unrealised gains; the 'alphanumeric' vs 'numeric' split reported is caused by the minus sign, not a mix of data kinds.

fundrate is a signed funding-rate figure; negative values indicate a negative funding rate and positive values a positive one. The reported numeric/alphanumeric split is an artifact of the minus sign, not two different data kinds.

priceshiftday is a signed daily price-change figure; negative values indicate a price decrease and positive values an increase. The reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not two different data kinds.

mkteffect is a signed market-impact figure; negative values indicate a downward market effect and positive values an upward one. The reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not two different data kinds.

slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative values indicate slippage in one direction (e.g. favorable) and positive values the opposite. The reported format split is caused by the minus sign, not two different data kinds.
feecoin records the currency in which feetotal (and rebtotal) is denominated, with observed values USDT, USD and USDC.

The business term 'trading fees' corresponds to feetotal/feerate; the fees table keeps rebate amounts in separate rebtotal/rebrate columns, so rebates are not part of 'trading fees' unless explicitly combined.

cancelnote is populated only for executions that ended in cancellation (values Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is empty for executions that were not cancelled, which is about 24.4% of rows.
exectune records whether an execution was a Maker or Taker fill; it is empty (31.1% of rows) when the execution did not result in a fill.

claims.statement: One row represents one account-balance record (a snapshot of a single user's wallet/available/frozen/margin and realised/unrealised lines), identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row represents one system-monitoring snapshot (API/queue/latency/websocket state), identified by systemmonitoringpivot, and each such row ties to exactly one analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row represents one analytics snapshot pairing exactly one marketdata record and one marketstats record from the same moment, identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row represents one fee (or rebate) event charged against an order, identified by feesnode; an order can have more than one fee row since the link to orders is many-to-one.
One row represents one execution (fill or cancellation) event against an order, identified by orderexecmark; an order can have multiple execution rows since the link to orders is many-to-one.
One row represents one market-statistics snapshot (funding, volume, supply, liquidity metrics), identified by marketstatsmark, tied one-to-one to a marketdata record via mdlink.
One row represents one market-depth snapshot, identified by marketdatanode.
One row represents one risk/margin assessment tied to an order, identified by riskandmarginpivot; an order can have more than one assessment row since the link to orders is many-to-one.
One row represents one order; orderspivot (and the alternate key recordvault) uniquely identify the 999 order records in this table.
One row represents one user, identified by userstamp (and the surrogate usersnode); there are 776 distinct users in this table.

The users table does not cover every user who appears elsewhere: about 22.3-22.4% of the user identifiers referenced from orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag have no matching row in users, so joins to users will silently drop roughly a fifth of orders and balances.
Wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum for all non-zero rows; it should not be summed alongside availsum or frozensum or amounts will be double counted.

Execution time (exectimespan) equals API latency (apilatmark) plus queueing (queueline) for 90.1% of non-zero rows; for the remaining ~9.9% exectimespan exceeds that sum, meaning an additional, unrecorded component contributes to execution time on those rows and the apilatmark+queueline breakdown understates it there.
Realised profit and loss is stored in accountbalances.realline as a signed amount: positive values mean realised gain, negative values mean realised loss.

unrealline holds signed unrealised profit-and-loss amounts: positive values are unrealised gains and negative values are unrealised losses, not two different kinds of data despite the mixed numeric/alphanumeric shape detected.

fundrate is a signed funding rate; negative values indicate a negative funding rate rather than a different kind of value, so it still measures the same quantity despite the mixed numeric/alphanumeric shape detected.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change; negative values mean the price fell that day and positive values mean it rose.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio; negative values indicate slippage in the opposite direction from positive values, not a separate category of data.
mkteffect is a signed market-effect measure; negative and positive values denote opposite-direction effects of the same metric.
dealedge holds exactly two values, Sell and Buy, giving the side of the order.
orderflow holds exactly four order-status values: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, New.
ordertune holds exactly four order-type values: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, Market.
