claims.statement: One row of accountbalances represents one account-balance record, uniquely identified by accountbalancesnode.
One row of analyticsindicators represents one analytics-indicator snapshot, uniquely identified by analyticsindicatorsnode.
One row of fees represents one fee (or rebate) charge event, uniquely identified by feesnode.
One row of marketdata represents one market-data (order book depth) snapshot, uniquely identified by marketdatanode.
One row of marketstats represents one market-statistics snapshot, uniquely identified by marketstatsmark.
One row of orderexecutions represents one execution (fill or cancel) event against an order, uniquely identified by orderexecmark.
One row of orders represents one order, uniquely identified by orderspivot, and equivalently by the natural key recordvault; the table contains 999 such orders.
One row of riskandmargin represents one risk/margin profile record, uniquely identified by riskandmarginpivot.
One row of systemmonitoring represents one system-monitoring snapshot, uniquely identified by systemmonitoringpivot.
One row of users represents one user, uniquely identified by usersnode and equivalently by the natural key userstamp; the table contains 776 such users.

The users table covers only 776 distinct users. About 22-22.4% of the user identifiers referenced from orders.userlink and accountbalances.usertag do not exist among these 776 users, so the table omits a sizeable share of the users who are active elsewhere in the data.

The orders table has 999 rows, one fewer than the other satellite tables (accountbalances, analyticsindicators, marketdata, marketstats, orderexecutions, fees, riskandmargin, systemmonitoring), which each have 1,000 rows, so orders is not populated to the same row count as the rest of the dataset.
dealedge records the side of the trade: Sell or Buy.
orderflow records the order's lifecycle status: New, PartiallyFilled, Filled, or Cancelled.
ordertune records the order type: Market, Limit, Stop, or StopLimit.
timespan records the order's time-in-force code: GTC, GTD, FOK, or IOC.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
feerange records a fee tier label (Tier1-Tier4) applied to the charge.
feecoin records the currency in which the fee amount is denominated, and varies by row across USDT, USD, and USDC.
cancelnote records the reason an order was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested) and is blank for the roughly a quarter of executions that were not cancelled.
exectune records the execution role, Maker or Taker, and is blank for about a third of execution rows where the role does not apply (e.g. no fill occurred).
wsstate records the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
acctscope records the user's account type: Spot, Futures, or Options.

Despite being declared as text(6), fundspot actually stores full timestamp strings (e.g. '2025-02-19 10:29:46'), with only 8 distinct hourly values, indicating it marks a snapshot time rather than a short code or price.

realline (realised profit and loss) holds signed decimal values, including both positive figures (gains) and negative figures (losses); the two 'format classes' seen in checks are simply positive vs negative numbers, not two different kinds of data.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) holds signed decimal values, including both positive and negative figures, the two 'format classes' being just the sign of the number.
fundrate is a signed decimal funding rate that can be positive or negative; the two 'format classes' in the check reflect sign, not distinct data types.
priceshiftday is a signed decimal daily price change that can be positive (price up) or negative (price down); the two 'format classes' in the check reflect sign, not distinct data types.
mkteffect, though declared as an integer column, actually stores small signed decimal fractions (e.g. -0.0001), so it behaves as a fractional market-impact ratio rather than a whole-number count.
slipratio is a signed decimal slippage ratio that can be positive or negative; the two 'format classes' in the check reflect sign, not distinct data types.
walletsum (wallet balance) is derived as availsum + frozensum, holding exactly for all non-zero rows; it is not an independent measurement.

exectimespan (execution time) equals apilatmark (API latency) + queueline (queueing) for about 90% of non-zero rows, but on the remaining roughly 10% of rows it is larger than that sum, implying an additional, unrecorded time component for those rows.

'Trading fees' (feetotal) are recorded in whichever currency feecoin specifies for that row (USD, USDT, or USDC); the term is not expressed in one common currency, so summing feetotal across rows without grouping by feecoin mixes units.

'Wallet balance' (walletsum) is defined only as available (availsum) plus frozen (frozensum) funds; it excludes margin funds (margsum) and realised/unrealised P&L (realline/unrealline), which are stored separately.
'Realised profit and loss' (realline) includes both gains and losses, represented as positive and negative values respectively, with no apparent floor.

'Execution time' is only fully explained as 'API latency' (apilatmark) plus 'queueing' (queueline) for about 90% of rows; for the remaining ~10% of rows it includes extra time beyond those two components, so the term cannot be assumed to be limited to those two factors in every row.

claims.statement: One row is one account-balance snapshot record for a user (wallet/avail/frozen/margin amounts at a point in time); accountbalancesnode uniquely identifies the row.
One row is one analytics-indicator record tied to exactly one marketdata row and one marketstats row.
One row is one fee charge/rebate record, optionally tied to exactly one order via orderslink.
One row is one market-data snapshot (quote depth), independently keyed.
One row is one market-statistics snapshot, tied to exactly one marketdata row via mdlink.
One row is one order-execution (fill) event, tied to exactly one order via ordersmark.
One row is one order; orderspivot and the alternate key recordvault each uniquely identify the row (999 orders in the table).
One row is one risk/margin profile record, tied to exactly one order via ordervault.
One row is one system-monitoring snapshot, tied to exactly one analyticsindicators row via aitrack.
One row is one user; both usersnode and userstamp uniquely identify the row, 776 users total.

The users table does not contain every user referenced elsewhere: about 22% of the userlink values in orders and the usertag values in accountbalances point to user identifiers absent from users, so orders and balances exist for users outside this reference table.
dealedge records the trade direction of the order: Sell or Buy.
orderflow records the order lifecycle status: Cancelled, Filled, PartiallyFilled, or New.
ordertune records the order type: Stop, StopLimit, Limit, or Market.
timespan records the order's time-in-force policy: GTD, FOK, IOC, or GTC.
orderbase records the channel through which the order was placed: Web, Mobile, Bot, or API.
exectune records the liquidity role of the fill: Maker or Taker; it is blank for about 31% of execution rows, presumably fills where this role was not captured.

cancelnote records the reason an execution/order was cancelled (Expired, InsufficientFunds, UserRequested); it is blank for roughly 24% of rows, which correspond to executions that were not cancelled.
wsstate records the websocket connection state: Connected or Disconnected.
acctscope records the user's account/trading scope: Spot, Futures, or Options.
feecoin records the currency the fee was charged in: USDT, USD, or USDC.
feerange records a fee tier classification: Tier1 through Tier4.
realline (realised profit and loss) is a signed quantity: both positive values (gains) and negative values (losses) occur, not a magnitude-only measure.
unrealline (unrealised profit and loss) is a signed quantity, holding both positive and negative values representing paper gains and losses.
fundrate is a signed funding rate, taking both positive and negative values.
priceshiftday is a signed daily price change, taking both positive and negative values.
mkteffect is a signed market-impact measure, taking both positive and negative values.
slipratio is a signed slippage ratio, taking both positive and negative values (favorable and unfavorable slippage).
wallet balance (walletsum) is a derived total equal to availsum + frozensum; it holds for all 1,000 non-zero rows, so summing walletsum together with availsum/frozensum double counts.
The business term 'wallet balance' is defined as available funds plus frozen funds (availsum + frozensum); it does not include margsum (margin balance), which is a separate figure.

execution time (exectimespan) equals API latency (apilatmark) plus queueing (queueline) for 90.1% of non-zero rows; for the remaining rows exectimespan exceeds that sum, meaning at least one further, unrecorded component also contributes to execution time.
'Execution time' is not fully explained by 'API latency' plus 'queueing' alone: for about 9.9% of rows a further, unmeasured time component is included in execution time.
'Trading fees' refers to feerate/feetotal (the commission charged); rebrate/rebtotal record a separate rebate credit and are not part of the fee amount.

Not every order execution row carries a maker/taker tag or a cancellation reason: exectune is blank for 31.1% of rows and cancelnote is blank for 24.4% of rows, so analyses keyed on either column silently exclude those executions.

claims.statement: One row represents a single account-balance record (a snapshot of a user's wallet, available, frozen and margin sums at one point in time).
One row represents a single analytics-indicator record that pairs one marketdata snapshot with one marketstats snapshot.
One row represents a single fee charge (or rebate) record associated with one order.
One row represents a single execution (fill or cancel) event belonging to one order.

One row represents a single order; orderspivot is the declared primary key, while recordvault is a distinct unique value per row that other tables (fees, orderexecutions, riskandmargin) reference as the order's business key.
One row represents a single market statistics snapshot for a market, linked to one marketdata snapshot via mdlink.
One row represents a single market data (order-book depth) snapshot.
One row represents a single risk-and-margin profile record attached to one order.
One row represents a single system-monitoring snapshot, each linked one-to-one to a distinct analyticsindicators record via aitrack.
